author: lu_pinto
content: I'm unsure whether that thread talks about `gasLeft` tracked at transaction level or frame level. My proposal does not change anything. `gasLeft` has frame scope, so you are impacted by the 63/64 rule same as today. So I don't understand how is one arguing that gas mechanics are changed. On mainnet we already have state gas component debited from `gasLeft` we just don't say it.

author: draganrakita
content:
From PR:
> Replaces the two-pool reservoir model with a single gas_left that both gas dimensions charge against. The EIP-7825 cap is enforced by a counter (tx_execution_gas_used) rather than by partitioning tx.gas
From discord: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1504670813339652169/1570022855868153880
> Why initial combined execution+state gas without reservoir would break. You send combination and track exec gas in global in background. In case of exceeding exec gas, revert whole transaction.

It is same proposal on how to handle gas. One of attack vectors is that someone can grief you and spend all execution gas.

author: lu_pinto
content:
I see, that clicked for me now. Yeah you can halt the tx fully that way and grieve gas when `gas_left > TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT` this is the actual problem. If you go lower than that there is no problem.

But I acknowledge that any attempts to workaround that are again going into gas mechanic changes territory which could break txs.

author: lu_pinto
content: Nonetheless I made some changes to the proposal <@429719902363058177>  - what if you make the `TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT` follow the 63/64 rule same as `gas_left`, for execution only? So no one can grief on the whole limit, so the parent will still have some runaway left.

content: You still get into edge cases where GAS shown you can do something, but in reality you OOG
